The code matches PRECOMMIT_DF6 on every point I checked: conventions, kvals, G6, H1-H7, tiers and selection. The result "0 configs survive (tier 1 = tier 2 = 0)" is robust. Every one of the 47 N1 passers fails H4 under the locked radius of 0.10 (I recomputed this from the stored N1 gates). All 47 also fail H6, H7 and G6, and the G6 margins are far from the threshold: drawdown margin at most 4.0% where 10% is needed. All of the following I confirmed by my own computation:
- G1-G5 recomputed from the df6_main rows give exactly 47 (single-gate counts 167/132/96/72/91); report 52; negative controls 0.
- The k values recomputed from the raw Ken French zips match df6_k.json exactly.
- N3, N4 and NA shifts give exactly the target daily Sharpe ratios.
- The DF5 parity harness re-runs at 0.0.
- Offset 0 reproduces reb_every bit-for-bit in REAL, P and X.
- Saturdays are compounded correctly in G6, and the G6 result reproduces.
- Report-only k* = 1.164 confirmed (fails at 1.155, passes at 1.165).
- Selection and stability code run without error.
The post-lock diff is report-only. The final.log traceback line numbers match the locked file, so gates, H tests, tiers and selection in df6_final.json came from the locked code.
Two caveats:
1. One claimed number is wrong: 38 of the 47 fail H5, not 34. Nine pass N2.
2. The N1 count of 47 is mostly an effect of the N1 convention. N1 sets DEF3's mean equal to the S&P mean in each world. In the crash-free X world that adds +1.44%/yr to DEF3; in REAL and P it removes 0.84 and 0.37. Under raw data only 11 of the 47 pass G4 (X30), so the drop from 47 to 9 under N2 happens entirely in the X world. This convention was pre-registered (inherited from DF5), so it is not a code bug, and it cannot change the "0 survive" result.

issues.what: N1 convention (DEF3 arithmetic mean set equal to the S&P mean in each world) boosts DEF3 by +1.44%/yr in the crash-free X world: raw DEF3 mean 15.19% vs S&P 16.63%. In REAL and P it lowers DEF3 by 0.84 and 0.37 %/yr. Implied DEF3/S&P daily Sharpe ratio under N1 is REAL 1.294, P 1.297, X 1.209; raw is 1.425, 1.356, 1.075. Most of the 47 N1 passers therefore depend on the X-world boost.

That equals the total N2 count of 9, so P30/P10 cause no N2 losses. Moving from N1 to N2 lowers X30 median CAGR by 1.02pp on average. N1 was pre-registered (DF5 convention), and H5 is the planned check against it.

issues.what: The expense ratio is counted twice from 2002 to 2014. The STAP/HLTH/UTIL series are actual XLP/XLV/XLU adjusted-close total returns from 2002, which are already net of the fund fee, and the code subtracts ER 0.15% again. N1, N3 and NA re-centre the mean, so only N2 (H5) is affected: about 0.07%/yr on DEF3, at most about 0.06%/yr on the portfolio.

DEF3 shows more positive autocorrelation than the market (variance ratio 1.50 vs 1.39), so monthly k is lower than daily k: 1.135 vs 1.181. issues.what: The negative controls are not matched on volatility. N1 mechanically rewards low-volatility sleeves (equal mean, lower vol, higher Sharpe), and ENER, MANU, FIN and SHOP are higher-vol sleeves. So 0/576 does not separate a 'defensive' effect from 'low vol plus mean matching'. UTIL (pre-1986 k_s 0.862) passes 36 under N1, which shows N1 passes follow 1986-2014 volatility, not pre-1986 Sharpe evidence.

How robust is the top config's N1 pass? Path sampling is not the risk: G2 and G4 hold in 98.7% of 1,000 path resamples. The risk is the DEF3 mean assumption.
- Margins under N1: P30 pair +1.195pp, X30 pair +1.710pp, REAL excess +2.493pp. Drawdown margins against the 10% requirement: REAL 0.248, P30 0.191, P10 0.166, X30 0.131, X10 0.116.

- Lowered by 1.0pp/yr: fails G3 (P10 pair -0.092). Break-even is about 0.89pp/yr, which matches the report-only k* = 1.164. X10 drawdown fails at about 1.25pp and P30 pair at about 1.45pp.
- N1 is optimistic. It implies DEF3's Sharpe is 1.29x (REAL), 1.30x (P) and 1.21x (X) that of S&P, above the pre-1986 k_s of 1.135. N3(k_s) is about N1 minus 1.0pp/yr, and under it the top config fails.
- In X, N1 lifts DEF3 1.44pp/yr above raw. With the shift calibrated in P and applied unchanged in X, the top config fails X10 drawdown (0.092) and the R63 config fails the X30 median.

Things working against the candidates (none changes the tier-0 outcome):
- G6 fails only because of the 10% margin. The candidate is directionally better on every G6 metric.
- Two rejections are hairline: H5 for the top config and H6 for the R63 config.
- 0.15% expense ratio is double-counted on the 2002-14 ETF segment of the sleeve files. It is too small to flip H5.
- H7's k_low is the minimum of four noisy estimates, so it is strict by construction.

E4, theory. In 1986-2014 NDX and SPX have the same Sharpe (P 0.445 vs 0.444; X 0.91 vs 0.92). With a sleeve at Sharpe parity (k=1), a static mix with less than 1x NDX exposure must repay the dropped (1-e)·mu_NDX from its own premium. The only extra returns are diversification and less volatility drag. At Sharpe parity with no frictions, that is worth +0.94%/yr (P30) and +1.60%/yr (X30). The same diversification is what gives the 0.17-0.18 ddm margin, because DEF3 fell only 0.25x as much as NDX on its worst days.

Real frictions then take it back. Fund fees plus the dividend tax cost 1.1-1.3%/yr. Capital-gains tax and trading costs cost a further 0.1-0.6%/yr. After them the paired margin is -0.36%/yr in P30 and -0.28%/yr in X30, and X30 ddm is 0.097.

So the return gates need a sleeve Sharpe premium of about k ≈ 1.16 (k* for the top config is 1.164). N1 grants 1.21-1.30. Pre-1986 the point estimate is 1.135 and k_low is 0.943. The drawdown side depends on DEF3 not crashing with tech, which held in 2000-02 but not in 1929-32, 1937-42 or 1973-74 (corr 0.79-0.86, worst-day ratio 0.62). Without a Sharpe premium the mix cannot beat QQQ on both return and drawdown in all three bases. Even the 1928-85 additive premium (NA) leaves only a knife-edge.

- Grid: 322 unique main configs (TQQQ 96, QLD 70, five a=0 points).

- Top config REAL/P30/X30 numbers and its G6 numbers (real path and OLD6), reproduced independently by repro.
- Report-only k* = 1.164.
- All 47 fail H4 (recomputed by audit and gates).
- All 47 fail G6. Me: recomputed the R2885 real path for all 47; none meets the 10% drawdown rule (largest margin 0.040; 0.0 difference from stored).
- Post-lock change is report-only (code diff plus hashes). Me: PRECOMMIT_DF6.md sha256 5fbb6548... also matches the registered value.
- X world matches its description. Me: excluded windows run peak to trough plus 250 days for 1987, 2000-02 and 2007-08; 0 sampled days fall inside them.

Only read-checked:
- H1, H2, H3 results for 45 of the 47.
- OLD6 for 44 of the 47 (does not matter, since the real path already fails).
- H6 and H7 flags for the 47. Simulated for only 2-4 configs, but backed by k* (1.11-1.17) being above k_s and k_low, and by the limit verifier's fine-grid search.
- Full-grid counts N3low/NA/N4 = 0.
- Report-sleeve and negative-control counts: gates were recomputed from stored rows, but the rows were not re-simulated.
- Data layer inherited from DF5: every verifier used the same input panels.

Contradicted:
- "34 also fail H5" is wrong: 38 of the 47 fail H5 and 9 pass, which equals the N2 count.
- The claim also leaves out the H1 (1), H2 (10) and H3 (5) failures. Neither error changes any tier.

(2) No verifier flagged changes_conclusion = true. I tested the issues most likely to flip the result:
- H4: the 7 configs that fail only H4 among H1-H5 have neighbour pass shares of 33-53% against the 75% required. The closest (9/17) would need 4 neighbours to flip, and I re-simulated its 8 failing neighbours: all fail again.
- G6: none of the 47 pass on the real path.
- Off-grid NA sliver: post hoc and not on the locked grid.
- Double-counted expense ratio: too small, and H4 fails regardless.
None of these is credible as a conclusion-changer.

(3) Still unverified that matters for the user statement:
- The DF5 data layer: synthetic TQQQ/QLD before launch (3r - 2rf - 2.45%), the KF-to-XLP/XLV/XLU splice in 2002 (with the expense ratio counted twice), and the tax engine. These are shared inputs, so no DF6 verifier checked them independently.
- The user-facing horizon tables. /tmp/df6w/top_conv_horizons.json is an extra post-hoc author file.

The tier-0 conclusion does not depend on any of these.

(4) VERDICT
The statement is supported, but it must carry these qualifiers:
- (a) "47" is in-sample. REAL, P and X are all built from the same 1986-2014 data, and the DEF3 region was picked after DF5 had seen that data. So these are not three independent confirmations.
- (b) "47" depends on N1, the DF5 convention. N1 implies DEF3 has a Sharpe 1.21-1.30 times the S&P's, and in X it adds +1.44%/yr to DEF3.
  - Raw 1986-2014 data: 9 pass.
  - Pre-1986 point estimate (k_s = 1.135): 4 pass.
  - k_low, NA or k = 1: none pass.
  - The top config needs k >= 1.164.
- (c) The 47 are one narrow diagonal band of neighbouring weights, not 47 separate methods.
- (d) Tier 2 = 0 rests on H4 alone for 7 configs, but by wide margins. Only relaxations that were not pre-registered (radius 0.05, or a 50% share) would create one tier-2 config, TQQQ R252 e0.60 c0.75, and it still fails H6, H7 and G6.
- (e) G6 fails on a 10% drawdown margin measured at -92% in the Depression, which is demanding. But the limit verifier's post-1933 windows show the mixes falling further than unlevered BusEq, so the pre-1986 rejection is real: DEF3's low correlation with tech (0.61 in 1986-2014) did not hold before 1986 (0.79-0.86).
- (f) H6 and H7 only move DEF3's mean and can only reject. G6 is the one test of the whole structure in another era.
- (g) Results are in USD, after the modelled Korean tax and costs; the tax on currency gains is not modelled.
- (h) Correct the H5 count to 38 of 47.
